cells.tense: The pieces of this are present to you now, and your hand is on them.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take a tangled thing and work it on paper toward its own logic, until what follows is a single step.
cells.core:
You can tell what deserves your attention, and in this stretch the pieces fit together without strain — decisions come quickly because what's on the table is visible at once. That alignment is why the hours run clean.

Put the pattern somewhere it can be read. When something is tangled, work it on paper to its own logic rather than the conclusion you'd prefer; the one step that actually follows will show itself. A single thing this week is enough to have its shape on a page. Standing far enough outside it to sketch it is what keeps this steady — closer in, you'd be trusting an impression.

cells.tense: The ending hasn't happened yet, and you're already living past it.
cells.act: begin the thing while it is still nothing in particular
cells.ask: Start a small first move with no name on it and no plan, and leave what it is undecided for a day.
cells.core:
A fragment comes in and the rest of the story assembles itself, so the present gets treated as something to get past on the way to what you've decided is coming. That speed is real. It's also running ahead of what's actually in your hands — you're bracing at a moment that hasn't arrived.

Go where you can't see instead. Start something while it's still nothing in particular and hold off on deciding what it is — a day, no label. The freshness that keeps getting reached for sits underneath what a thing gets called, not after it. Let something stay new a little while before you settle what it is.

cells.tense: A door opened and closed, and you've stayed on this side.
cells.act: name the form it will take, and only that
cells.ask: Take something you keep circling and put down a line: its shape, nothing about why or how it ends. Then stop there.
cells.core:
You register what matters, and that hasn't gone anywhere, but it's aimed at nothing in particular and doesn't land. Some step went by and you stayed where you were, watching well, arriving nowhere. The watching goes out; little comes back.

Start smaller than the situation feels like it deserves. Put down a line naming the form of the thing you keep circling — the shape of it, nothing about why or how it ends. That's the whole act. Return tends to come through the smallest concrete thing you're willing to hold, not through effort aimed at this directly. Give a single thing its form and the rest has somewhere to attach.

cells.tense: You are the one watching, and it's filed under how things are.
cells.act: let this moment be a fresh entry, not a continuation
cells.ask: Next time you clock what's going on around you, let it arrive as new rather than the next beat of what was already known.
cells.core:
People lean on something quiet in you: you register what's happening in a place before anyone says so. You'd call it being observant, or say the situation was obvious. What catches all of it stays unnamed, and what gets called circumstances is partly that attention choosing where to point.

Test it once. The next time you notice what's really going on, let it come as something arriving now rather than the next beat of what was already known. Same noticing, one difference: you're inside it. Nothing else has to change. What watches doesn't need defending or a better name, only to be known as the one doing it.

attempts.check: The record doesn't say any process of understanding has run to completion in this person's life, and 'nothing left to see' is a reader-facing claim the cell can't support — a reader could rightly say they're mid-sort, not finished. The asks survive being wrong because each is one small act they can do regardless of whether the read lands: writing a line, starting a thing before it's named, refusing to decide a form, standing at the door as it opens.
